sources.method: width = 25.4*D*a/sqrt(a^2+b^2), height = 25.4*D*b/sqrt(a^2+b^2), rounded half-up to 0.1 mm. D = 6.9 in, a:b = 1080:2640 taken exactly from resolution_px (square pixels assumed); the published diagonal is assumed exact (OEMs round it). Computed by scripts/device-registry-derive.py; re-run it after editing either input.

notes: US name 'motorola razr - 2025' and global name 'motorola razr 60' are ONE physical device: motorola.com/us .../razr-gen-5/pmipmhv41mo names the Device 'motorola razr - 2025' and motorola.com/we .../razr-60/pmipmhv41mm names it 'motorola razr 60', and both pages publish identical dimensions (73.99 x 171.30 x 7.25 / 73.99 x 88.08 x 15.85) and 188 g; the product codes differ only in the final character (pmipmhv41mo vs pmipmhv41mm). Motorola prints the 2025 dimension triples UNLABELLED and width-first ('Open: 73.99 x 171.30 x 7.25mm'); mapped here as width 73.99 / long-axis height 171.30 (open) and 88.08 (closed) because 73.99 is the value common to both states and because Motorola's 2026 pages label the same shaped triple explicitly 'H x W x D'. The US page prints a stray character ('7.25mmc') in the open depth; the value read is 7.25 mm. Display resolutions are recorded [width, height]; Motorola writes the main panel as '2640 x 1080' (height-first) and the cover panel as '1056 x 1066' with no orientation stated, so the cover pair is recorded in Motorola's own order. mass_g 188 is Motorola's 'About 188g'. Both refresh rates are Motorola's 'Up to' maxima. announced/released are from Motorola's own April 24, 2025 press release read via a web.archive.org snapshot dated 2025-12-13 (motorolanews.com returns HTTP 403 to direct fetching); the May 15 on-sale date is the US date. hinge.crease left null - Motorola never states 'teardrop' or 'U' anywhere on these pages. max_angle_deg not published. || EVIDENCE SWEEP 2026-09-13: these values were present in the research pass but carried NO sources[] entry covering their field, so they were set to null per the registry rule (a value without a citation is an assertion, not evidence). Preserved verbatim here so a human can re-source rather than re-research: hinge.type = 'flip'; hinge.axis = 'short'.
